classification.difficultyReason: Uses a general binomial expansion and coefficient comparison to prove why the middle-term splitting method works.

answer.short:
$a=pr$, $b=ps+qr$ and $c=qs$.

Expand the product and compare coefficients.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(px+q)(rx+s)&=prx^2+psx+qrx+qs\\(px+q)(rx+s)&=prx^2+(ps+qr)x+qs\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients with $ax^2+bx+c$ gives
$$a=pr,\qquad b=ps+qr,\qquad c=qs.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence show that if $ax^2+bx+c$ can be factorised, then $b$ can be written as the sum of two numbers whose product is $ac$. (This shows why our method of factorisation works.)

answer.short: The two numbers are $ps$ and $qr$: their sum is $b$ and their product is $ac$.
answer.worked:
From part a, $b=ps+qr$, so the two numbers are $ps$ and $qr$. Their product is
$$\begin{align*}(ps)(qr)&=pqrs\\(ps)(qr)&=(pr)(qs)\\(ps)(qr)&=ac.\end{align*}$$
Thus $b$ is the sum of two numbers whose product is $ac$, as required.
